title: Fuselage — Aft Lower Shell Longitudinal Joints — Re-Sealing and Drain Grommet Installation

issue.reason: Initial issue of the re-sealing and drain grommet bulletin for early-build aircraft.

abstract: Retrofit of the interim sealing standard on early-build aircraft: the longitudinal joint sealant of the aft lower shell is replaced by a high elongation grade and three drain grommet positions are opened at each joint land.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft from the first two production batches showed sealant blistering along the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell at their first scheduled structural check, with standing moisture found in the joint land on three of them. This bulletin brings those aircraft to the interim sealing standard already cut in on the production line, before the blistering has a chance to turn into corrosion under the joint.
sections.description: The longitudinal joint sealant between stations C52 and C66 is removed and replaced by a higher elongation grade applied as a fillet, three drain grommet positions are opened at the low point of each joint land, and the inner doubler is re-primed on removal and refitted.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the aft cargo compartment and lift the cargo floor panels between stations C52 and C66. Remove the inner doubler D5331120951225 and the local stringer run D5331122551549 and record any corrosion finding before further work. Remove the old sealant from the joint land by non-metallic scraper only. Open the three drain grommet positions at the low point of each joint using the drill template supplied with the kit. Re-prime the doubler and the stringer land and install washers AGS334024-84 at each grommet position. Refit the doubler and stringer and apply the fillet seal. Do a water drain check with the aircraft on jacks in the level attitude. Install the cargo floor panels and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft MSN C00001 through C00145 that were not brought to the interim sealing standard in production. Aircraft delivered from MSN C00148 onward were built to that standard and are not in the effectivity.
sections.material_note: Kit K5331-1008-01 contains the sealant, the primer, the grommet set and the drill template. One kit is needed per aircraft and the kit lead time is twelve weeks.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled structural check of the aft lower shell, and not later than 48 months from the date of this bulletin.

title: Fuselage — Aft Lower Shell Longitudinal Joints — Re-Sealing and Drain Grommet Installation

issue.reason: Bulletin withdrawn on the issue date of the doubler campaign, with the remaining operators directed to that campaign instead.

abstract: Cancelled bulletin that re-sealed the aft lower shell longitudinal joints and added drain grommets on early-build aircraft, withdrawn once the corrosion-resistant doubler standard replaced the sealing approach entirely.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft from the first two production batches showed sealant blistering along the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell, with standing moisture found in the joint land on three of them. This bulletin brought those aircraft to the interim sealing standard. It is cancelled because the sealing approach was itself replaced by a titanium doubler with an open drain path, and an operator who embodies this bulletin now has to undo most of the work to reach the current standard.
sections.description: The longitudinal joint sealant between stations C52 and C66 was removed and replaced by a higher elongation grade applied as a fillet, three drain grommet positions were opened at the low point of each joint land, and the inner doubler was re-primed on removal and refitted.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the aft cargo compartment and lift the cargo floor panels between stations C52 and C66. Remove the inner doubler D5331120951225 and the local stringer run D5331122551549 and record any corrosion finding before further work. Remove the old sealant from the joint land by non-metallic scraper only. Open the three drain grommet positions at the low point of each joint using the drill template supplied with the kit. Re-prime the doubler and the stringer land and install washers AGS334024-84 at each grommet position. Refit the doubler and stringer and apply the fillet seal. Do a water drain check with the aircraft on jacks in the level attitude. Install the cargo floor panels and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to aircraft MSN C00001 through C00145 that had not been brought to the interim sealing standard in production. Aircraft delivered from MSN C00148 onward were built to that standard and were never in the effectivity.
sections.material_note: Kit K5331-1008-01 contained the sealant, the primer, the grommet set and the drill template. Kits are no longer supplied and the residual stock has been scrapped. An operator holding an unopened kit returns it under the commercial terms of Service Bulletin CRN-53-1042, which is the campaign the remaining pre-cut-in aircraft now go to; an operator part way through this bulletin stops at the next convenient check rather than completing it, because the doubler installation removes the sealant and the grommets again.

type_data.compliance_time: Cancelled. No further embodiment is recommended; the remaining effectivity is covered by Service Bulletin CRN-53-1042.

revision_history.reason: Bulletin cancelled on the issue date of CRN-53-1042; effectivity closed and kit supply ended
